findings.title: Checkout and order history act on whatever customer_id the caller sends

failure.trigger: An unauthenticated attacker calls POST /checkout?customer_id=<victim>&use_wallet=true, or GET /orders?customer_id=<victim>, cycling through customer IDs
failure.what_breaks: Neither endpoint checks who is calling, so the attacker spends any customer's wallet balance and reads every customer's order history
failure.who_notices: Customers whose balances drain, then support, and possibly a regulator if order data counts as personal data

findings.fix: Authenticate every request with a dependency that resolves the customer from a verified session or token, and remove customer_id from the request entirely so it cannot be supplied by the caller.

findings.title: Checkout cannot recognize a repeated request
findings.evidence: def checkout(customer_id: str, amount_cents: int, use_wallet: bool = False):

failure.trigger: The client's request times out after the card was charged, and the mobile app retries checkout
failure.what_breaks: The second request is treated as a new purchase: the card is charged again and a second order is created
failure.who_notices: The customer, on their card statement, then support and finance

findings.fix: Require an Idempotency-Key header. Insert (customer_id, key, request_hash, status='in_progress') under a unique constraint before any side effect; on a repeat, replay the stored response or return 409 while in progress.

findings.title: Card charge is retried with no idempotency key sent to the provider
findings.evidence:
for attempt in range(5):
    resp = requests.post(PAYMENTS_URL, json={...})

failure.trigger: The provider charges the card, but the connection drops before the response arrives
failure.what_breaks: The loop treats the lost response as a failure and charges again, up to five times for one checkout
failure.who_notices: The customer, who sees up to five identical charges

findings.fix: Send an Idempotency-Key header derived from the checkout's key on every attempt, so the provider deduplicates the charge. Only then is retrying safe.

findings.title: Wallet balance updated with read-modify-write
findings.evidence:
wallet = db.query(Wallet)...first()
if wallet.balance_cents < amount_cents: ...
wallet.balance_cents -= amount_cents

failure.trigger: Two checkouts for the same customer run at the same moment (double tap, two devices, or a retry)
failure.what_breaks: Both read the same balance and both pass the check; one debit is lost or the wallet pays for two orders with money for one
failure.who_notices: Finance, during reconciliation, as unexplained negative balances

findings.fix: Debit atomically: UPDATE wallets SET balance_cents = balance_cents - :amt WHERE customer_id = :id AND balance_cents >= :amt, and treat rowcount 0 as insufficient balance.

findings.title: Card is charged before the order is safely recorded
findings.evidence:
charge = charge_with_retry(...)
order = Order(...)
db.add(order)
db.commit()

failure.trigger: The database commit fails after a successful charge (deadlock, connection drop, deploy restart)
failure.what_breaks: The customer has been charged, but no order exists and nothing records that a charge happened
failure.who_notices: The customer, who paid and received nothing

findings.fix: Record the checkout's progress (the idempotency row) before charging, write the order and the charge ID in one transaction after the charge, and run a reconciliation job that matches provider charges to orders and refunds orphans.

findings.title: Order commit and 'orders.paid' event are not atomic

failure.trigger: The broker is unavailable, or the process is killed between the commit and the publish
failure.what_breaks: The order is saved as PAID but the event is never sent, so fulfilment and the confirmation email never happen
failure.who_notices: The customer, whose paid order never ships

findings.fix: Write the event to an outbox table in the same transaction as the order, and publish it from a separate relay. Make consumers idempotent on order_id.

findings.title: The amount to charge comes from the client
findings.evidence: def checkout(customer_id: str, amount_cents: int, use_wallet: bool = False):

failure.trigger: A logged-in customer edits the checkout request and sends amount_cents=1 for a cart worth 50,000
failure.what_breaks: The server charges 1 cent, then saves the order as PAID for the full cart, so the goods ship almost free
failure.who_notices: Finance, when order totals stop matching revenue

findings.assumption: The order is for server-side items with known prices (a cart or product catalog), not a free-form amount such as a top-up or donation
findings.fix: Accept a cart or order ID, load the line items and prices on the server, and compute amount_cents there. Never read a price, total, or discount from the request.

findings.title: Payment provider call has no timeout

failure.trigger: The payment provider stops responding without closing connections
failure.what_breaks: Python requests waits indefinitely, so every checkout worker blocks until the server has no workers left and the whole API stops responding
failure.who_notices: Every user of the API, and the on-call engineer

findings.fix: Pass timeout=(3, 10) (connect, read) on every call, or configure it once on a shared requests.Session.

findings.title: Retries use a fixed 1-second sleep with no jitter

failure.trigger: The payment provider has a brief outage during peak traffic
failure.what_breaks: Every in-flight checkout retries in lockstep each second, multiplying load on the provider while it tries to recover
failure.who_notices: All customers checking out, as the outage lasts longer than it needed to

findings.fix: Use exponential backoff with full jitter, capped (for example random.uniform(0, min(4, 0.5 * 2 ** attempt))), and cap total attempts at 3.

findings.title: Failure to publish the order event is silently ignored

failure.trigger: publish() raises because the broker is down or misconfigured
failure.what_breaks: The API returns success, no log or metric records the lost event, and the problem is invisible until customers complain
failure.who_notices: Customers, days later, when orders do not arrive

findings.fix: Remove the bare except. With the outbox fix (ST-006), publishing moves to the relay, which retries and alerts on failure.

findings.title: Order list loads every order for the customer

failure.trigger: A large business customer with hundreds of thousands of orders opens their order history
failure.what_breaks: The request loads every row into memory, the worker runs out of memory or times out, and the endpoint fails for that customer

findings.fix: Paginate with a server-enforced maximum page size, using keyset pagination: WHERE id > :after_id ORDER BY id LIMIT :limit.

findings.title: Declined cards and bad requests are retried

failure.trigger: The provider returns 402 card declined, and raise_for_status() raises an HTTPError, a subclass of RequestException
failure.what_breaks: The declined card is retried five times, adding about five seconds of delay and five declined attempts that can trigger the issuer's fraud checks
failure.who_notices: The customer, whose card may be blocked by their bank

findings.fix: Retry only connection errors, timeouts, and 429/502/503/504. Return other 4xx responses to the caller immediately.
